It then applies `uniform_dyadic_integral_tails` and closes each shell with `gaussian_bochner_shell_bound`. The file contains no second proof, so nothing inside it can repeat.

It does not share a nontrivial block with the target proof.

The only overlap is the pattern of building a summable shell majorant and feeding it to a dyadic-tail lemma. That pattern is already factored into the shared lemmas in `SummableShellTail` and `GaussianLinearGrowth`. The remaining glue is routine argument passing, which the rubric excludes. So there is no justified repeated-machinery finding.
